- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The harp is one of the most iconic instruments in traditional Irish music and has been an integral part of Irish culture for centuries.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The harp is often considered the national symbol of Ireland and is featured on the country's coat of arms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In traditional Irish music, the harp is usually played as a solo instrument or as part of an ensemble with other traditional instruments such as the fiddle, accordion, and tin whistle.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Popular tunes that feature the harp include "The Lark in the Morning," "Planxty Irwin," "Carolan's Concerto," "Brian Boru's March," and "The Fairy Queen."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The harp provides a unique sound and brings a sense of beauty and elegance to the music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Modern musicians who incorporate the harp into their Irish music include Moya Brennan, Cormac De Barra, Aine Minogue, Janet Harbison, and Gráinne Hambly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Moya Brennan is a member of the band Clannad and incorporates the harp into her solo recordings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cormac De Barra blends traditional Irish music with elements of jazz, classical, and world music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Aine Minogue has released over a dozen albums in the traditional Celtic genre.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Janet Harbison is a classically trained harpist and composer.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Gráinne Hambly is known for her expertise in traditional Irish music.
